# I Don't

## Bayesian inference

Suppose we have some data $\mathbf X = X_1, X_2 \dots X_n$. 

We also have a model that relates our data to some model parameters via a likelihood function $f(x | \theta)$. 
We have some prior probability distribution $\pi_0(\theta)$ encoding our a priori belief about where/how $\theta$ might be distributed.

We can encapsulate our belief about the parameter in the posterior probability distribution:

$$\pi(\theta|\mathbf X) = \frac{\pi_0(\theta) \cdot f(\mathbf X | \theta) }{\int \pi_0(\theta) \cdot f(\mathbf X | \theta) d\theta }$$

## Things we might be interested in

### The probability density

This posterior probability density we saw is in general intractable, because we don't (currently) have any idea about the integral term in the denominator.

### The marginal likelihood

The denominator term is a really useful thing to have because it quantifies the *marginal likelihood* or *model evidence*. This essentially tells us how well our model fits the data. 

$$p(\mathbf X | \mathcal M) = \int_{\theta \in \Theta}  f(\mathbf X | \theta, \mathcal M) \cdot \pi_0(\theta | \mathcal M)  d\theta$$

### The posterior mean
$$\mathbb E_{\theta \sim \pi(\cdot|\mathbf X)} [\theta]$$



## Other things we might be interested in

### The posterior variance
$$ \mathbb E_{\theta \sim \pi(\cdot|\mathbf X)} [\theta^2] - \big(\mathbb E_{\theta \sim \pi(\theta|\mathbf X)} [\theta]\big)^2$$

### Extreme value probabilities
$$\mathbb P (\theta > c | \mathbf X) = \mathbb E _{\theta \sim \pi(\cdot|\mathbf X)}[\mathbb I(\theta > c)] $$

### Expectations
In general we want to evaluate expectations wrt the posterior .

## Another thing we might want

### Posterior predictive distribution
$$\mathbb P(y| \mathbf X, \mathcal M) = \int_{\Theta} f( y |\theta, \mathcal M) \cdot \pi(\theta| \mathbf X, \mathcal M) d\theta $$

## Monte Carlo Integration

Suppose we have $N$ i.i.d. samples $\theta_1, \dots \theta_N$ from a distribution with density $f(\theta)$.

By the law of large numbers, we can get a consistent estimator of the expectation of any function $a(\theta)$ w.r.t. $f$.

By the law of large numbers, as ${n\rightarrow \infty}$:

$$ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} a(\theta_i) \rightarrow \mathbb E_{\theta \sim f(\cdot)}[a(\theta)] $$
